milestone: A CONFIRMED Pulse authorization whose historical snapshot predates structured extraction gets one live, read-only reread to establish receipted evidence for the first time — without being routed through reconciliation, which requires a baseline to already exist.
problem: Running the acceptance test's own script (scripts/materialize-pulse-evidence.ts) against Nakamoto's real row surfaced a genuine architecture gap: the row was confirmed via the pre-structured-extraction prose classifier, so its persisted partnerStatus snapshot carries no pulseEnrolled/pulseCommitmentRecorded field to materialize from. Materialization correctly refused (NO_HISTORICAL_SNAPSHOT) rather than fabricating evidence. But the natural next suggestion — 'use the ordinary verify/reconcile path if fresh partner evidence is wanted', which materialize's own refusal message says — turned out not to cover this case either.
observedFailure: verifyHorizenTransparencyActivation (the live verify-and-transition path) deliberately excludes CONFIRMED from RECONCILABLE_STATES, so it structurally refuses to touch Nakamoto's already-CONFIRMED row at all.

reconcilePulseConstitutionalState (the live reconciliation path) CAN run against a CONFIRMED row, but only to compare a fresh read against evidence that must already exist — it refuses NO_RECEIPTED_EVIDENCE when there is nothing to compare against, which is exactly Nakamoto's situation. Neither of the two existing live-capable functions can establish a first-ever baseline for a legacy CONFIRMED row.
rootCauses: materializePulseEvidenceFromHistoricalConfirmation and reconcilePulseConstitutionalState were both designed against an implicit assumption that never held for a legacy row: that a CONFIRMED row's structured facts are recoverable either from its historical snapshot (materialize) or from a comparison against already-existing evidence (reconcile). A row confirmed before structured extraction existed satisfies neither assumption — there was no third function for 'no baseline exists yet, and no historical snapshot to recover one from, so make exactly one live call to establish one.'
resolution: Added bootstrapPulseEvidenceFromLiveReread (services/horizen/authorizationClient.ts), deliberately NOT folded into reconcilePulseConstitutionalState, per the operator: keeping it a separate, explicitly-named function preserves reconciliation's own contract ('compares a fresh read against an existing baseline') rather than overloading it with a second, unrelated 'there IS no baseline yet' case.

Preconditions: the row exists and is CONFIRMED (STATE_MISMATCH otherwise); no canonical receipted evidence exists yet at record.receiptRef (checked via the existing getPulseAuthorizationEvidence read — reused, not duplicated). Existing evidence makes this an idempotent no-op (alreadyBootstrapped:true) with NO live call made.

Makes exactly one read-only get_onboarding_status call, against the row's OWN recorded network (record.network) rather than trusting a caller-supplied one that might differ — a mismatch refuses WRONG_CHAIN before any live call happens.

pulseEnrolled and pulseCommitmentRecorded are gated independently, reusing buildPulseVerifiedEvidence and createActivityReceipt exactly as writeConfirmedPulseActivation/materializePulseEvidenceFromHistoricalConfirmation already do — a read that supports enrollment but not commitment mints only pulse_enrollment_verified.

pulseEnrolled===true is a hard precondition for minting anything. false live-contradicts the row's own CONFIRMED state (PULSE_NOT_ENROLLED_LIVE, refused rather than silently resolved either way); anything else (no structured field at all) is AMBIGUOUS_LIVE_STATUS, refused rather than guessed. A thrown transport/tool error is caught and returned as an explicit TRANSPORT_FAILURE refusal rather than propagating an exception.
Never signs, submits, re-enrolls, or writes `state` — the row is CONFIRMED before this runs and CONFIRMED after, on every path including refusal. Never invokes reconciliation.

9 tests added to tests/horizen-authorization-client.test.ts covering the operator's full named scenario list: confirmed+no-receipts (both the STATE_MISMATCH refusal and the proceeds-to-live-call path), already-bootstrapped, enrollment-only, enrollment+commitment, negative, ambiguous, wrong-chain, and transport failure.
Shipped with scripts/bootstrap-pulse-evidence.ts, mirroring scripts/materialize-pulse-evidence.ts's CLI shape, for the operator to run against Nakamoto's live row.
rejectedApproaches: Widening reconcilePulseConstitutionalState to also handle the 'no evidence yet' case (bootstrap on first call, compare on later calls) — rejected per the operator's explicit instruction to implement a separate, explicitly-named function, so reconciliation's contract stays exactly 'compares two existing things' and the bootstrap function is named for what it actually does.

Re-contacting Horizen inside materializePulseEvidenceFromHistoricalConfirmation itself when the historical snapshot has nothing to recover — rejected: that function's own contract is 'never live, never a rewrite' (see its own header); conflating it with a live path would blur the exact distinction the operator drew between the two same-day acceptance-test functions.

Letting a transport exception from the live get_onboarding_status call propagate as an uncaught error (matching verifyHorizenTransparencyActivation/reconcilePulseConstitutionalState's own pre-existing behavior, which do not wrap that call in try/catch) — rejected specifically for this new function because the operator's spec named 'transport failure' as one of the required test scenarios with an explicit refusal outcome, not a thrown exception.
